claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my one child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or enrolled on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me when Alex left school or finished his education? Specifically, was it recent (within the last few months), and has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for training or work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a few months back, but no, he hasn't signed up with any careers service or anything like that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning does he live with you and do you contribute to the cost of looking after him (such as food, clothes, or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me at home and I support him - I pay for his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One more important question:

Do you live in the UK, and are you either a British or Irish citizen, or do you have the right to live and work in the UK (for example, through settled or pre-settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He has left school and is not currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training
- He has not registered with a careers service or similar organisation
- You live in the UK and are a British citizen
- You are responsible for Alex and he lives with you

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19, but only if they:
- Remain in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels or NVQs up to level 3), **or**
- Are on an approved training course, **or**
- Have recently left education and registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation

Since Alex has left school, is not in qualifying education or training, and hasn't registered with a careers service, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria.

**What you could do:**
- If Alex enrols in full-time non-advanced education or an approved training course, you may become eligible again
- If Alex registers with a careers service or similar organisation, you may be able to claim for a limited period while he looks for work or training

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, you're welcome to check your eligibility again.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has left school. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 only if they remain in full-time non-advanced education (e.g., A-levels, NVQs up to level 3) or are on an approved training course. Alternatively, a child who has recently left education may still qualify for a limited period if they register with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for training or work. Since Alex is not in qualifying education or training, and has not registered with any careers service, he does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit eligibility.
